newsitem.title: USA: Ohio Senate passes Cleveland school takeover bill.
newsitem.headline: Ohio Senate passes Cleveland school takeover bill.

text.p: The Ohio Senate Wednesday approved a bill enabling Cleveland Mayor Michael White to take control of the city's public school system.

The bill, which had been approved earlier by the House, must now be returned there for technical reconciliations before it can be forwarded to the governor, said Mike Dawson, a spokesman for Gov. George Voinovich.
White said the vote was "another step forward" in reforming the schools, but would reserve further comment until it is signed by the governor.
Ohio Department of Education has overseen the financially strapped district since March 1995 and Ohio Auditor Jim Petro has declared a fiscal emergency for the district.
Voinovich said in a statement that the legislation would provide an opportunity for a public-private partnership to aid the schools and also provide accountability for the system.

An aide to one of the bill sponsors has said it was patterned after Illinois laws permitting Chicago Mayor Richard Daley to take control of the Chicago Public School system, streamline operations, balance the budget and launch a five-year $806 million bond-funded capital improvement program.
